A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SiameseNorm research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original 1.3B language-model pretraining results, downstream evaluations, component ablations and analyses of training dynamics.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, MoE and vision experiments, depth studies, layer-pruning tests and warm-up stress tests.

M1.justification: The coupled streams, shared residual blocks, normalized-input mechanism and depth-wise scaling remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 restates the earlier forward equations. Applying the previously described construction to additional model families does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds ImageNet image classification and image generation, plus C4 validation for layer-pruning analysis. FineWeb-Edu training and the existing language benchmark suite are retained. This substantially expands the represented data and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated Peri-LN and SpanNorm baselines across all three existing 100B-token learning-rate regimes, including convergence and divergence outcomes. The previous comparators remain, substantially extending the normalization comparisons.

E3.justification: New protocols include approximately 390M-parameter models with four depth-width configurations trained for 12B tokens, and 15A2B MoE models trained for 100B tokens. v2 also introduces shortened/absent warm-up tests, individual-layer removal, and vision evaluation using Top-1 accuracy and FID. The original 1.3B settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds fixed-parameter depth-width comparisons, direct layer-utilization tests through pruning, and warm-up stress tests separating topology robustness from residual scaling. Table 3 adds the Siamese ablation lacking both auxiliary mechanisms. The earlier sub-stream comparison is retained as appendix Table 4.

E5.justification: Neither version documents seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Existing shaded training plots retain the same reporting practice; the additional results do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All 23 shared Table 1 rows retain their values. New results include MoE PPL of 7.92 for Pre-Norm versus 7.76 for SiameseNorm, DeiT-S accuracy of 79.8 versus 81.3, and DiT-L/4 FID of 45.21 versus 41.34. v2 also adds depth, pruning, warm-up, ablation and overhead findings, while dropping the earlier qualitative observation of increased massive activations.

T1.justification: The forward equations and Jacobian derivations are retained. However, Section 3 removes the deduction that subsuming component architectures makes their best performance a lower bound on SiameseNorm's achievable performance, and replaces the categorical prevention-of-vanishing-gradients assertion with a narrower identity-route statement. No new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand the contribution from 1.3B language-model validation to improvements across dense models, MoE, vision and diffusion, emphasizing compatibility with standard Pre-Norm recipes without architecture-specific tuning. They also temper the earlier categorical reconciliation and structural-impossibility claims.

C2.justification: New depth, pruning and warm-up interpretations provide more direct arguments for layer utilization and topology-specific robustness. v2 removes the explicit qualification about exhaustive learning-rate tuning for fair comparison. It also replaces v1's limitations concerning uneven downstream gains and massive activations with an appendix limitation about missing rigorous theoretical explanations and convergence guarantees.

D1.justification: Appendix Table 6 adds a full MoE configuration, including 24 layers, 96 experts, top-8 routing, scheduling and auxiliary-loss weights. v2 quantifies training-speed and memory overhead and updates aggregate compute from over 50,000 to over 60,000 A100 hours. Dense-model settings and code access remain unchanged, although the earlier explanation of gamma initialization is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for SpanNorm, GatedNorm, MoE architectures and the new evaluation domains. It explicitly credits depth scaling and normalized input as established auxiliary mechanisms. The central positioning against ResiDual and Hyper-Connections remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and substantial theoretical and experimental prose are rewritten. Auxiliary mechanisms move into Section 3, topology and auxiliary ablations become separate subsections, and the sub-stream comparison moves to the appendix. The conclusion and limitations are separated, with funding and impact statements added.

P2.justification: Figure 2 expands into a full-width three-panel display with pruning results. Table 1 gains baselines and a MoE setting; new tables present depth/vision results and MoE configurations. Forward equations become Algorithm 1, the ablation table expands, and the earlier sub-stream table moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the paper's central evidence through direct pruning and warm-up tests, controlled depth comparisons, additional baselines and validation beyond one dense language-model family. These address important weaknesses in generality and mechanism support. Removing the massive-activation and uneven-gain caveats reduces transparency, and vision protocols remain terse, but the stronger validation and more restrained theoretical assertions provide a substantial net improvement.
